evidence.requirements: Met: start page with heading, links named exactly by `name`, family, L3, Search that finds '7,62 x 51', Family select and count (app.js:66-103, list.jpg). Detail view has the meta list, water capacity with its source link, Symbol/Value/Unit tables grouped by section, Print button, 'All cartridges' link and a hash route that survives a reload (app.js:107-215). The drawing is inline SVG at 1 unit = 1 mm with outside view, hatched section, dash-dot axis, all required dimensions and a title block. Print is one A4 page with a footer (print-308_win.jpg). Partly met: (1) 'scales to the width of a phone screen'. The SVG has `min-width: 560px` inside an `overflow-x:auto` figure (app.css:161-168), so on a phone it scrolls sideways instead of scaling. (2) 'Labels do not overlap each other or the outline'. Every horizontal label sits on its own dimension line, so the line runs through the text (y+1 baseline, drawing.js:187-189: 'L6·71.12' in detail-308_win.jpg, 'L3-19.15·-0.25' in detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). 'R 1.37', 'R 1.09 -0.18' and 'R 1.52 -0.25' are cut by their extension lines. The vertical lane labels are crossed by the P1/H2 extension lines (E1 in detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, P2 in detail-308_win.jpg). (3) α is labelled with an arc that spans only α/2 and floats inside the bullet near the cone apex, away from the shoulder (drawing.js:193-221; on 9,3 x 74 R the label sits above the bullet tip). (4) The title block always says 'Scale 1:1' (drawing.js:274), but the drawing is shown at a different size on screen and on paper.
evidence.correctness: Geometry follows the rules closely. The chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (geometry.js:165-169). Rimfire half-round radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) with its apex at R1/2 (158-164). Groove: floor e min, ramp to (P1/2,E); belt ramp at δ to R3/2, then to E and a step in (185-207). Body, shoulder and neck follow the rules, with r1 min and r2 fillets (210-232). Bullet s, k and m match rule 7, and the tangent ogive centre is correct (86-124, 270-297). Heel at H2-2tb (276-277). Walls tn and tb and w (234-260) are correct, and pocket sizes are right (model.js:14-22). Proportions match the reference drawings for 308, 300 Win Mag, 9 mm and 22 LR. Values, tolerances ('39.62 -0.2') and angles ('10°58'00"') are shown as specified. Print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg). Defects: the α arc measures the half angle while its label reads the included angle α, and it sits in the bullet with no cone lines to the apex. Dimension lines strike through their labels, and diameter extension lines run across the whole profile and through the lane labels. 'Scale 1:1' is untrue as displayed. On straight cases the wall tapers linearly from tb to tn over the whole body (geometry.js:247-248), which is an interpretation of rule 8. w also adds bodyStart+tb, a term the brief does not list (260).
evidence.security: DOM is built with createElement/textContent (app.js:26-43). The only innerHTML is the SVG string (app.js:181), and every data string in it goes through escapeHtml (drawing.js:189,220,243,255,270-272,286-287). rec.key goes into the pattern id unescaped (drawing.js:133), but it is static data. No eval, no fetch, no external resources. The browser test asserts zero non-file requests (browser.test.js:132-135).
evidence.code_quality: Small, clear modules: format, model, geometry (pure {z,r}), drawing and app. The naming tracks the brief's rules, and rule numbers appear in the comments. Missing values are collected and shown (geometry.js:135-142, app.js:183-188). Drawbacks: many magic layout constants in drawing.js. Label boxes are estimated from a fixed glyph width (GLYPH 0.56). Section headings are raw field ids. There is dead code in the browser test: page.evaluate runs before goto, inside a .catch (browser.test.js:86,99).
evidence.tests: node:test units cover format (angles, units, symbols, tolerances), model (rim type, pockets, sections, Tol folding, search, filter counts, routes, capacity) and geometry for each family (chamfer, groove, belt with δ, rimmed step, rimfire half-round, bullet factors for pointy, rounded, flat and SWC, heel, walls, w, pocket, α apex, fillet). Drawing tests check label/label and label/outline overlap, viewBox containment and title block position for all 25 records. Playwright checks the list, search, routes and reload, a one-page PDF for all 25, phone overflow, dark scheme and no network. Gaps: the overlap tests ignore dimension and extension lines, and they rely on estimated text boxes. So the visible strike-throughs pass. Nothing checks the α arc or the scale.
evidence.ux_design: The list is dense and clean (list.jpg). On the detail view the drawing is capped at 760px. Long rifle drawings come out small with ~14px labels (detail-308_win.jpg). Short cases are blown up so that labels and the title block are huge (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg), which makes the views inconsistent. Strike-through labels and long parallel extension lines over the bullet make the drawing harder to read than the reference. The tables are clear, with right-aligned tabular numbers, but section headings are camelCase ids ('caseHead', 'junctionCone'). The print layout is good: drawing at full width, three columns of tables, footer (print-308_win.jpg). Dark mode is defined in CSS (app.css:14-24) but there is no screenshot of it.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img, aria-label '<name> drawing' and a <title> (drawing.js:285-287). Tables have th scope=col and scope=row (app.js:142-153). The inputs have <label for> (97-98), the count is aria-live, html has lang=en, and there is a :focus-visible outline (app.css:65). Native links, button and select are keyboard-usable. The text alternative for the drawing is only the name, but the tables carry the values. Muted grey #5d636c on white passes contrast.
evidence.simplicity: No runtime dependencies. About 900 lines of plain JS and one CSS file, which fits the problem. Playwright is the only dev dependency. No needless abstraction: a small h() helper and IIFE modules on window.CIP.
evidence.maintainability: The README has open, develop and layout instructions, and package-lock.json is present. engines node >=22. Tests share the same files through a vm loader. But the README points to docs/superpowers/specs/...design.md, which is not in the delivered repo. There is no CI configuration, no .nvmrc or exact Node pin, and no changelog or release process beyond version 1.0.0. The browser tests need a manually available Chromium.
evidence.visual_design: Calm, neutral typography with tabular numbers and consistent muted labels. The look is plain but tidy (list.jpg, detail-*.jpg). Weak points: labels sit on their dimension lines, title block and label sizes swing between cartridges, and the print table headers render larger than the body rows ('Symbol Value Unit' in print-308_win.jpg, because rem is not scaled in print). Monospace section headings clash with the sans-serif body.
evidence.layout: Clear order: toolbar, name, three-column meta grid, drawing, then cartridge and chamber tables in two columns. On desktop the drawing uses only about 60% of the content width for rifle cases, while a short case gets a title block that dominates the page (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg). In 308 the P2 lane label reaches the title block edge (detail-308_win.jpg). There is no clipping, and print is well packed onto one page.
evidence.usability: Few steps: search or filter, click a name, back with 'All cartridges'. The list keeps its search and filter state (app.js:23-24). There are an empty-state message, a not-found view and a one-click Print. On phones the drawing must be scrolled sideways. The α annotation is hard to find on long-shoulder cases.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data tables and the fidelity to the published values, and the one-page print sheet is useful. But the drawing, the centrepiece, falls short of drafting practice: labels struck by their lines, an α arc that does not mark the angle it names, a wrong '1:1' scale claim and inconsistent sizes. It reads as a competent prototype rather than a polished reference.

unmet_requirements: Drawing does not scale to phone width: min-width 560px with sideways scroll (app.css:161-168)
Labels overlap lines: dimension lines run through every horizontal label, extension lines cross R and the vertical lane labels (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg)
Shoulder angle α is shown by a half-angle arc inside the bullet near the cone apex, not clearly dimensioned at the shoulder
Title block always says 'Scale 1:1', which is not the scale shown on screen or in print
strengths: Geometry implements the brief's rules faithfully for every family (chamfer, groove, belt at δ, rimfire half-round, fillets, bullet s/k/m and tangent ogive, heel, walls, solid head, primer pocket), with matching unit tests
Data is shown as published: tolerances next to values, angles as d°mm'ss", correct symbols and units, all sections in Symbol/Value/Unit tables, and a reload-safe hash route

Plain, dependency-free app that works from file://, plus a one-page A4 print with header, full-width drawing, three-column tables and source footer, checked by a Playwright PDF test for all 25 records
issues: Drawing legibility: horizontal labels sit on their dimension lines, and diameter extension lines run across the profile and through the lane labels. The overlap tests miss this because they only check the outline.
Shoulder angle and scale are misrepresented: the α arc spans α/2 inside the bullet, away from the shoulder, and the title block always claims 'Scale 1:1'
Inconsistent and non-responsive drawing size: long cases are small, short cases have oversized labels and title block, and phones get a 560px sideways-scrolling drawing instead of scaling to width
review.verdict: The data handling, geometry rules and print layout are solid and well tested, so the database is trustworthy as a table reference. The drawing, though, has labels struck through by their lines, a misleading α arc and a false 1:1 scale, and it does not scale on phones; it needs another pass before publishing to a technical audience.
